cues.text: Let us work through a simple example to see how return on investment and payback period are calculated.
Suppose a project costs twenty million naira.
Over the chosen period, it produces thirty million naira in measurable benefits.
In this case, the return on investment, or ROI, is fifty percent.
If the annual net cash savings from the project are five million naira, then the simple payback on the twenty million naira investment is four years.
That is, it takes four years of those savings to recover the original cost.
It is important to remember that these are simplified measures.
They ignore discounting, which means they do not account for the time value of money.
They also ignore uncertainty about whether the expected benefits will actually be achieved.
So, when you use them, compare alternative projects over consistent periods, so that the comparison is fair.
And do not rely on the financial figures alone: include the non-financial outcomes as well.
